title: Echo and Orbit Anew
premise: Gideon Halloran, a clone created to inherit his original's unsolved murder case, works the shipping lanes between two colonies that severed contact after a war neither will name. When the freighter Perihelion returns from deep space with its crew biologically younger than when they left, Gideon discovers the ship's jump drive can rewind time — and that both colonies' governments knew. The murder he inherited was committed to bury this secret, and the killer is still aboard the corridors of power. As the jump window closes, Gideon must choose which colony's frozen population wakes first, knowing one choice erases the other from history — and that justice for his original means dooming half of humanity.
about_author: Jude Galloway is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent eleven years relaying messages between ships that never met. They write about distance, inheritance, and the people who carry other people's unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Gideon Halloran pilots a mail-and-freight run between the silent colonies of Meridian and Cael Harbor, carrying letters no government will transmit. His POV establishes the loneliness of the route and the murder case file he inherited with his original's memories. Beat: weary competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Inherited Ghosts
chapters.summary: Flashback-adjacent chapter: Gideon reviews the case file of Halloran Prime, murdered nine years ago mid-investigation. He remembers the crime scene as if he stood there, because in memory, he did. Beat: the uncanny intimacy of borrowed grief.

chapters.title: Signal from Nowhere
chapters.summary: A distress ping arrives from coordinates where nothing should be: the Perihelion, declared lost twelve years ago. Gideon diverts against protocol. POV shifts briefly to the ship's AI, which logs an impossible crew manifest. Beat: dread sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Everyone Aboard Is Younger
chapters.summary: Gideon docks with the drifting Perihelion and finds thirty-one crew members alive, healthy, and years younger than their service records. Captain Ilsa Voss doesn't remember the last decade at all. Beat: wonder curdling into wrongness.

chapters.title: The Case That Fits
chapters.summary: Back at Meridian station, Gideon cross-references the Perihelion with his original's final investigation: Halloran Prime interviewed Voss days before dying. The murder and the lost ship are the same story. Beat: the thrill of a pattern emerging.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, No Words
chapters.summary: Gideon travels to Cael Harbor under false papers to access sealed naval archives. We see the cold war between colonies through border inspections and propaganda murals. Beat: paranoia as atmosphere.

chapters.title: The Archivist Who Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: In the archives, Gideon meets Sefa Oyelaran, an archivist who recognizes him — not as Halloran Prime, but as someone she met on the Perihelion before it launched. She has been waiting nine years for him to come looking. Beat: vertigo; the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: What the Drive Does
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the truth in fragments: the Perihelion tested a chronal jump drive that displaces biological time backward while the universe moves on. The crew aged backward because they jumped too deep. Beat: revelation delivered like a confession.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Both governments have known about the drive since before the war. The silence between the colonies isn't diplomatic — it's containment. Anyone who learns the truth dies. Beat: the scale of the conspiracy lands.

chapters.title: The Murder, Replayed
chapters.summary: Gideon finally understands what his original found: evidence linking the drive program to a planned mass cryosleep selection. Halloran Prime died for a list. Gideon carries the list in his own head without knowing it. Beat: horror of self-discovery.

chapters.title: Voss Wakes Up
chapters.summary: Captain Voss, recovering in quarantine, begins remembering fragments her rewound brain suppressed — including a face she saw the night Halloran Prime died. Her POV. Beat: fragile alliance forming.

chapters.title: The List in His Head
chapters.summary: Under Sefa's guidance, Gideon attempts controlled memory excavation to recover the names his original hid. The process is painful and incomplete. Beat: vulnerability; identity as contested territory.

chapters.title: Meridian Sends for Him
chapters.summary: Meridian intelligence summons Gideon home with suspicious courtesy. He realizes his diversion to the Perihelion tripped every alarm. Beat: the hunter becoming the hunted.

chapters.title: Deputy Director Crane
chapters.summary: Introduction of Antagonist Crane, who runs the containment program and speaks to Gideon with unsettling warmth — he helped design the cloning project that made Gideon. Beat: charm as threat.

chapters.title: Offered a Place in the World
chapters.summary: Crane offers Gideon legitimacy: full citizenship, the case closed, a life. All he must do is hand over the recovered names and forget the Perihelion exists. Beat: temptation framed as belonging.

chapters.title: What Clones Are For
chapters.summary: Gideon learns clones were commissioned specifically to inherit dangerous knowledge — living dead-drops. His entire existence is a storage solution. Beat: existential rage.

chapters.title: Running the Dark Lane
chapters.summary: Gideon refuses and flees Meridian through unpatrolled space, Voss and the youngest crew member, pilot Juno Reyes, aboard. A chase sequence through debris fields. Beat: kinetic escape, loyalty forged under fire.

chapters.title: Cael Harbor Opens a Door
chapters.summary: Unexpectedly, Cael Harbor grants Gideon asylum — because their intelligence wants the drive too. He trades sanctuary for archive access. Beat: uneasy bargains; no clean allies.

chapters.title: The Cryosleep Vaults
chapters.summary: Gideon tours Cael's vast cryosleep vaults: four hundred thousand colonists in suspension, waiting for a future the colony can't afford to give them all. The drive could change that — or end it. Beat: moral weight made physical.

chapters.title: Two Lists
chapters.summary: The recovered memory yields not one list but two: populations selected by each government to wake after a single-use jump. Each side planned to save its own and erase the other. Beat: the theme crystallizes — justice outside the law vs. survival.

chapters.title: Juno's Question
chapters.summary: Young pilot Juno, aging backward still, asks Gideon whether a person who gets their years returned owes anything to the person they were. Her POV. Beat: thematic heart, small-scale mirror of the plot.

chapters.title: Voss Remembers the Killer
chapters.summary: Voss's suppressed memory surfaces fully: she saw Crane himself aboard the Perihelion's launch bay the night before departure — and saw him speak to Halloran Prime. Beat: the net tightening around the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Window
chapters.summary: Astronomical calculations confirm the jump window opens in nineteen days and closes forever after. Both colonies mobilize fleets toward the Perihelion. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Archive
chapters.summary: Cael authorities seize Sefa and the research, revealing they intend to use the drive exactly as Meridian would. Gideon escapes with only partial data and Juno. Beat: betrayal; the middle collapses.

chapters.title: Alone with the Choice
chapters.summary: Hiding in a derelict mining rig, Gideon confronts the arithmetic: the drive can wake one vault or none. Any third option is theory. Beat: despair before resolve.

chapters.title: Halloran Prime's Last Message
chapters.summary: A hidden layer in the memory excavation unlocks: his original anticipated death and recorded a message — not naming the right choice, but naming the principle: 'No list written by power survives contact with the people on it.' Beat: inheritance completed.

chapters.title: Stealing the Ship Back
chapters.summary: Gideon, Voss, and Juno infiltrate the impound yard and retake the Perihelion from joint colonial custody. Action set-piece. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Crane's Truth
chapters.summary: Cornered via comm channel, Crane argues his philosophy: someone must choose, neutrality is genocide by delay, and he chose to be the one who decides. Gideon hears his own doubts in the enemy's mouth. Beat: antagonist humanized, stakes clarified.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Sefa, freed by sympathetic archivists, transmits a discovery: the drive's displacement can be split across two shallower jumps — waking both vaults, at the cost of the crew aging further back, possibly to nonexistence. Beat: hope with a price tag.

chapters.title: Who Pays
chapters.summary: The Perihelion crew votes. Voss volunteers first; Juno, who has the most years to lose, insists loudest. Gideon refuses to decide for them — the anti-Crane move. Beat: loyalty vs. truth resolved at human scale.

chapters.title: Fleets in the Dark
chapters.summary: Both colonial fleets converge on the Perihelion's position. Standoff chapter told partly from a Meridian gunner's POV who hesitates to fire on a ship full of children. Beat: systems straining against conscience.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: Marines board; Gideon buys time by broadcasting the two lists — every selected name, both colonies — to every open channel. The secret dies in daylight. Beat: climax begins; truth as weapon.

chapters.title: Crane Comes Aboard
chapters.summary: Crane personally leads the assault, confronting Gideon in the jump chamber. Their argument becomes physical. Voss holds the drive interface. Beat: personal and political climax fused.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: With minutes left, Gideon makes the choice the whole book demanded: he initiates the split jump, letting the crew's sacrifice stand, refusing both lists. The drive fires. Beat: irrevocable action.

chapters.title: White Space
chapters.summary: Inside the jump, time behaves strangely: Gideon experiences fragments of both futures waking — both vaults opening, both colonies seeing the same sky. Whether real or projected, it sustains him. Beat: lyrical interlude, emotional peak.

chapters.title: What Came Back
chapters.summary: The Perihelion emerges. The crew survived, aged back to childhood — alive, remembered by no one but each other. Voss is a young woman with an old captain's eyes. Beat: bittersweet cost made visible.

chapters.title: Both Worlds Wake
chapters.summary: On both colonies, cryopods open simultaneously. Four hundred thousand people per side step into a world whose governments just fell. Gideon watches from orbit, anonymous. Beat: awe and aftermath.

chapters.title: The Trial That Isn't
chapters.summary: Crane survives, arrested not by any state but by a citizens' tribunal assembled from the newly woken — justice outside the law, literally. Gideon testifies as both witness and evidence. Beat: thematic resolution.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Epilogue-adjacent: months later, the colonies reopen communication, and the first transmission is a passenger manifest — the Perihelion's crew, offered passage home to two worlds instead of one. Beat: reconciliation earned, not given.

chapters.title: Echo and Orbit Anew
chapters.summary: Gideon takes the long route again, mail and freight, but now the lanes are talking. In his cabin, the case file sits closed beside a child's drawing Juno gave him. He is no longer anyone's copy; he is the man who carried it through. Final beat: peace as a chosen orbit.
